references.text: The place that the Lord chooses to have his name dwell there is the central theme in both texts—the chosen place of worship for God.
Addresses the situation when the place the Lord chooses is too far away, and gives instructions on how to handle offerings from a distance.
Passover sacrifice from small livestock and cattle at the place the Lord chooses to have his name dwell there—same terminology and theme.
Slaughtering of the Passover lamb at the place the Lord chooses—a parallel to slaughtering cattle and small livestock at the chosen place.
Instructions on eating the firstfruits of cattle and small livestock at the place the Lord chooses—the same context regarding slaughter and consumption.
Rules for slaughtering cattle, sheep, and goats—basic text that Deuteronomy 12:21 expands to allow slaughter outside the sanctuary.
Permission to slaughter and eat meat within the city gates according to one's desire—a direct parallel to eating in the city gates according to the soul's craving.
God's gift of animals to humanity for food—the basis for the Lord giving cattle and small livestock as mentioned in the verse.
